clips.title: The story
paras: In Dun Morogh, Alliance warlock novices face their first trial under Alamar Grimm. They gather magical feather charms from Frostmane troll novices before learning to summon an imp.

At Anvilmar, dark magic is tolerated out of necessity, though it is not openly celebrated. Alamar Grimm, an established warlock, pursues occult research in relative discretion. When a recruit shows raw promise, influential voices take an interest. Their pressure convinces Grimm to leave his studies and assess the novice himself.

Before teaching a novice to enslave lesser demons, Grimm demands proof of physical endurance and magical affinity. Frostmane troll novices gather in a cave southwest of Anvilmar, carrying primitive feather charms infused with subtle primal magic. The novice must defeat these magical adversaries and take their charms. The trial proves the novice can overcome a magical foe, while giving Grimm curious specimens for his research.

The charms satisfy Grimm that the novice has sufficient will to survive. He then teaches the summoning of an imp, the warlock's most basic minion. Grimm warns that an imp's small size hides chaotic fire magic, and an undisciplined master can easily be overpowered.

clips.title: Quest text
paras: You must be the new adventurer everyone's been whispering about. Must be someone's taken a liking to you if they've asked me to take time away from my research to start your training.
Don't worry, I won't hold it against you.
The simplest of the summoning spells you will learn is that of the imp. Before I impart this to you, however, you must prove that you have the necessary magical and physical ability.
Bring me three feather charms from the frostmane novices from the cave to the southwest.

clips.title: Progress
paras: Those feather charms the novices carry have some sort of magical power to them. It will be interesting to research them. I wouldn't have expected it from the trolls.

clips.title: Completion
paras: Very good, very good! You've done well, friend. Perhaps the interest that is being shown in you is deserved, after all.

That'll be for the others to decide--assuming your imp doesn't overpower you and nip your career in the bud. For now, I'm satisfied that you'll probably survive your first few months as an adventurer.
A word about the imp, friend. As a traveler knows, don't let its size fool you, its magic can be very dangerous.
